decisoes.title: Error messages: brand wine or a distinct error red?
decisoes.context: The brand KB: form errors use the brand colour, not red, because red is 'clínico demais'. The app's error token is brick #8B2420 (close to wine #651B19 but distinct).

options.desc: Errors stay distinguishable from primary actions (wine means 'act'); always paired with words.
options.label: Keep brick #8B2420

options.desc: Follow the brand rule; errors and actions share a colour, so wording carries the meaning.
options.label: Use wine for errors

decisoes.title: Adopt the brand's 'avoid' word list as an app copy rule?
decisoes.context: From the brand KB (VOZ/03-LEXICON): avoid burnout, esgotamento, sobrecarga, resiliente/resiliência, empoderamento, autoconhecimento, guerreira, forte (as an aspirational virtue). Also: no exclamation marks, no corrective sentences, 'reconhecimento, não correção'. All compatible with the spec.

options.desc: The nos-no-limiar agent flags any of these words in app copy.
options.label: Adopt as an app rule

options.desc: Agent mentions them as suggestions, never as 'corrigir'.
options.label: Advisory only

options.desc: Only the spec's own language rules apply.
options.label: Don't adopt

decisoes.title: Primary buttons: keep the pill shape?
decisoes.context: The brand KB says 'CTA primário nunca em pílula' (pills feel 'consumer demais'). The approved mockup and the app use wine pills for every primary action.

options.desc: The brand rule was written for social/print; the app follows the approved mockup.
options.label: Keep pills (mockup)

options.desc: Follow the brand rule: e.g. 12 pt corner radius on primary buttons. One token change, visible on every screen.
options.label: Switch to rounded rectangles

decisoes.title: Approve the 15 activity drafts?
decisoes.context: Titles and summaries come from the spec; the steps and variations were written by Claude and are marked 'rascunho' (spec §22: nothing is published by AI alone). File: src/data/activities.ts — or read them in the app under Explorar → Experimenta isso.

options.desc: List changes in the note.
options.label: Approved with edits — see note

decisoes.title: How is Mônica credited inside the app?
decisoes.context: Mônica is 'psicanalista clínica, graduanda em psicologia e autora'. The spec (§1.5, §9) says the app must not present itself as psychological care; showing a clinical credential inside the app can pull it toward CFP Resolution 9/2024 territory. Legal review (spec §9) is still pending.

options.desc: 'Conteúdo editorial de Mônica Tangerino, autora' — no clinical credential in app screens until legal review.
options.label: Credit as author only

options.desc: Show 'psicanalista clínica, graduanda em psicologia e autora' on the About screen.
options.label: Full credential in 'Sobre'
No personal credit in the app yet

decisoes.title: Does Mônica confirm 'the spec wins' over the mockup on conflicts C1–C12?
decisoes.context: Applied by default: tab 'Salvos' with a bookmark, no like counts, no search on Home, Home leads with 'Me tira do sofá', no 'planos' button, copy that doesn't presume loss, welcome without a photo. Full list: docs/design/mockup-v0-decomposition.md §6.

options.desc: Write in the note which conflict should follow the mockup instead.
options.label: Partly — see note

decisoes.title: What do I build next in the app (after the agents)?
decisoes.context: Onboarding and on-device saving are done. Remaining Phase 0 items you picked earlier.

options.desc: The phone still shows Expo's default icon.
options.label: App icon + splash with the logo

options.desc: 'Ainda gosto disso?' and 'Isso ainda é meu?' (spec §4.5).
options.label: Games A and B

options.desc: Protects 'Me tira do sofá' before it grows.
options.label: Automated tests for the matching logic

decisoes.title: How much of Mônica's thesis enters the app?
decisoes.context: The brand's thesis starts from 'sofrimento silencioso' and a clinical/psychoanalytic frame (Winnicott, Freud). The app spec forbids presuming suffering and clinical framing. Bridge: the book's 'reorganização' (saúde emocional 'habitável'), 'limiar', 'sustentar'.

options.desc: Spirit and vocabulary (limiar, habitável, reconhecimento); never suffering/clinical framing, never theory names in the app.
options.label: Background only

options.desc: Some world content (e.g. 'Quem sou eu agora?') adapts book passages, reviewed against the spec.
options.label: Also as editorial content

decisoes.title: Where does an agent package live (its source of truth)?
decisoes.context:
The agents product already has Agent Studio: versioned agents in the database, a 10-tab UI, publish gates with evals, and an import format (noctus.agent-bundle/v1). It has no export, no consumer API and no learnings store.
Our two new agents (mobile-dev, nos-no-limiar) are Claude Code advisors, a new kind next to the runtime agents Julia and IsaIA.

Your message "build them alike IsaIA" points to option 1 (authored IsaIA-style: sections + skills + knowledge + evals → bundle → Studio). Please confirm by deciding here.

options.desc: Authored and versioned in the Studio UI; repos receive an exported, pinned copy. One place to manage every agent.
options.label: Agent Studio (database) is the source

options.desc: products/agents/packages/<key>/ in the repo; Studio imports them for display and evals. Diff-friendly, but two places to look.
options.label: Git files in noc are the source

options.desc: Start file-based to unblock today, migrate to Studio when the export API exists.
options.label: Git now, Studio later

answer.note: Decided in chat 2026-10-03: git is the single source, IsaIA-style authoring (sections, skills, knowledge, evals) inside the agents product; one build produces both the Claude Code files and the Studio bundle; file updates must sync.

decisoes.title: How does a project (like limiar-app) consume an agent?
decisoes.context: A consumer repo needs the agent as files Claude Code can load: .claude/agents/<key>.md plus agents/<key>/ (knowledge, learnings).

options.desc: A command (noctus.dev MCP tool / CLI) pulls <key>@<version> from the agents product and writes the files into the repo. Reproducible, works offline, upgrades are explicit commits.
options.label: Pinned pull, committed

options.desc: A session-start hook downloads the latest published version. Always fresh, but needs network + token and can change under you mid-work.
options.label: Live fetch every session

answer.note: From chat 2026-10-03: Claude Code is the primary surface (your plan), so consumers hold committed, pinned files; sync runs on every push.

decisoes.title: How do learnings flow back into the agent?
decisoes.context: You chose: learnings are captured automatically as we work. The question is where they land and how they become part of the next agent version.

options.desc: Each consumer repo appends to agents/<key>/LEARNINGS.md in the same commit as the work. A push command sends new entries to the agents product, where they're reviewed in the UI and promoted into the next published version.
options.label: Local log, pushed upstream, promoted after review

options.desc: Sessions post learnings to the product API as they happen. No local copy; needs network every time.
options.label: Written straight to the agents product

answer.note: From chat 2026-10-03: learnings are written locally in the same commit and synced upstream on every push.

decisoes.title: How does a consumer repo authenticate to the agents product?
decisoes.context: Today every agents-product route refuses non-user callers (403 user_required). A pull or a learnings push from a repo needs some machine access.

options.desc: A pk_ token per consumer project with only agents:read (published packages) and learnings:write. Stored in the developer's local env, never committed.
options.label: Scoped project token

options.desc: The command opens a browser login like expo login did. No tokens to manage, but no automation (CI can't pull).
options.label: Your SSO login only

answer.note: Implied by 'sync on every push': a git hook can't do a browser login, so it needs a scoped token kept in local env (never committed). Reopen if you prefer otherwise.

decisoes.title: How should dev advisors sit next to runtime agents in Studio?
decisoes.context:
Julia and IsaIA are runtime agents (they chat with end users, have tools, evals). mobile-dev and nos-no-limiar are read-only Claude Code advisors used while developing.

Your message "build them alike IsaIA" points to option 1 (same registry, same bundle format). Please confirm by deciding here.

options.desc: agents.kind = runtime | dev-advisor. Same versions, sections, knowledge, audit log and UI; tabs that don't apply (Chat, Clients) hide for dev-advisors.
options.label: Same registry, a 'kind' field

options.desc: New tables and pages just for dev advisors. Cleaner separation, but duplicates versioning, knowledge and audit.
options.label: Separate registry

answer.note: From chat 2026-10-03: 'build them alike IsaIA' — same registry and bundle format, distinguished by a kind field.
